- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next 3–7 days; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
- If true price deviates from 30-day moving average by >3%, model often misjudges mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 30-day MA if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment <0.3 for 3+ consecutive days), model underperforms; add 1–3% to forecast to account for suppressed volatility.
- If model forecast is consistently 5–10% above true price for 3+ consecutive days, apply “sentiment lag correction”: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 5 days if sentiment remains low or neutral.
